Which quests should you skip?

  • Someone Needs A Lesson: Getting between Vasil and his dad gives Coen a chance to see other people's home lives, but doesn't factor into the broader plot.
  • On The Run: Finding Iorgu's pig lets Coen confront his feelings about bloodshed and the uncomfortable analogy of humans as vrakhiri livestock, but there's more pressing stuff in town during the prologue.
  • Into The Den: This one's not time-sensitive, so come back for it after the prologue.

1 Morning

Live Bait

Right after leaving Coen's house, walk down the hill to talk with your sister Yanna standing around with Lunka and Mirto.

  1. I've got time. I'll help you. Agree to escort them to the river to fish.
  2. Take your pick on how to respond when Yanna asks what their father would think.
  3. Do not waste time by playing tag with your siblings on the way. Tell them to stop complaining right now. Coen scolds them a bit harshly, but Yanna appreciates the backup.
  4. Choose either response when reminding Yanna not to go into the water.

Go find the four fishing rods stashed under a bush just northwest of where Yanna is standing and then place them in the four different pole spots along the bank. The choices in the next conversation don't have long-lasting effects, but there are subtle differences in how the siblings all interact and I think this is the best version:

  1. Tell Yanna "You should be. I might not be around forever." when talking about the worms before moving on to get a bit of extra conversation with Mirto, either to argue or level with him as you choose.
  2. Tell Lunka any opinion on whether worms are hurt by getting put on a hook, she's upset by it no matter what. Personally, I just own up that I don't know how worms feel.
  3. Say "You're upset by something else," when Lunka cries over the worms to get a shot at the most sibling reconciliation version of the conversation.
  4. Tell Mirto "I'll take care of you," to bring out his trust in Coen rather than deflecting to Anca or their mother.

Same goes for the conversation with Brencis's officer, the scummy jerk. You can get into a fight with him if you want, but I prefer not to. You can also get more lore out of the conversation with the Uriash guard that joins after.

  1. I don't know: Play dumb to keep the conversation from going sour fast.
  2. Why all this interest in my father? Again, this keeps things from escalating.
  3. Leave her out of this: Hold off on pulling your sword and another guard will interrupt before things get out of hand.
  4. No. Nothing of the sort. Tell the Uriash you don't know anything about rumblings of a rebellion (because so far you don't!)
  5. Then why do you serve the vrakhir? Ask the Uriash about his loyalty to get a surprisingly earnest answer about the power dynamics between them, humans, and vrakhiri.
  6. Thank you. I appreciate it. Respect the Uriash's show of kindness.
  7. Maybe they aren't all the same. Instill a bit of healthy solidarity in your siblings.

2 Morning

After you're done fishing, take a moment to wander around Laslea village picking up quests. Grab these quests, but don't pursue them yet:

  • Disturbed from Crina, the woman in the graveyard by the keep.
  • Blasphemy from Gremla, the woman in the village crying in front of onlookers.
  • Deep Down from Gavril working in his field on the way to the forest.
  • Do not chase down and tackle Vasil, the annoying lad insulting you around town. It takes time, and I recommend skipping that quest (Someone Needs A Lesson).

Dead Drop

After accepting a few quests, score some extra coins and loot by taking the small path up a hill directly east of Coen's house to the outcast's graveyard marked with a large, gnarly tree on the map.

  1. Inspect a grave in the north corner to learn more about Vasil (still not doing his quest though, sorry)
  2. Immediately behind the trees in the north corner, climb a ledge into a small cave to loot 37 Denarius, a regenerative salve, golden tableware (to sell), and an Amulet of Fortitude
  3. Back at the graves, inspect the one in the south corner to start the Dead Drop quest
  4. Use Coen's focus to follow the footprints and carvings up into the woods to a dead drop hidden under a tree where you'll loot a mysterious letter, Ring of Purging, 19 Denarius, and 100 XP

Withering Away

Next, head to Anca's house down the small western path out of town for the Withering Away quest to get herbs for Coen's mother as Pieter directed. Your choices here don't have any major impacts aside from Anca's immediate reaction to Coen's attitude. Here's what I consider the best options:

  1. Choose to [keep on looking] instead of calling out to Anca when you approach her to see an extra hint about her backstory, but don't press her about the scars right afterwards.
  2. Take your pick on how Coen reacts to Anca saying that he must be worried for his mother.
  3. "I understand", to pay Anca the double rate she requests, which she appreciates, since you can afford it after looting that cave.
  4. (Optional) "Gladly – I've missed it too," to stay with Anca for the Page-Turner quest, especially if you're interested in romancing Anca later.
    Otherwise, say "I really have to go" and you can spend an extra time slot elsewhere instead.

3 Noon

Page-Turner

Despite how the dialogue choice makes it look, this only takes one extra time slot, meaning your entire time with her to complete Withering Away and Page Turner together takes two time slots.

  2. Continue to insist with "This Catullus sounds more interesting." and then "You sound like your prioress." and finally "Thank you for not smacking me."
  3. As Coen reads, the correct translations are "Kisses" and "Grains of sand" though you're not penalised for guessing wrong first
  4. When you run outside to help Anca save the herbs in her shed, use Coen's focus and collect 11 dried herbs hanging from the ceiling. Including the herbs she already gave you for Coen's mother, you should have 12 dried herbs in your inventory before you talk to her again. You'll get slightly different dialogue choices depending on whether you saved them all or only some of them.
  5. When Coen cleans Anca's wound, either dialogue option for lowering or removing her shirt will wind up with topless Anca, so choose as you will
  6. "I enjoy the company more than the books." One more chance to get in a compliment for Anca before leaving.

4 Noon

Withering Away part 2

Herbs in hand, hurry back home to Coen's house. You'll witness a mysterious argument between Pieter and Vladimir, which we'll uncover more about later. For now, help Coen's dad brew Anca's recipe for Esme. Do not screw the recipe up or else things are going to go very badly for Coen's family at mass tonight. If you've forgotten what Anca said, it's:

  1. [use hot water]
  2. [add three spoonfuls of herbs]

After that, you can answer Pieter how you like about his training plans and then convince Esme to drink the brew. Then just say "Let's" to Pieter instead of pressing him to talk. Either is fine, really, but I like to think Coen understands what kind of man his father is.

DO NOT follow Pieter to go train together up the hill. Don't worry, he'll wait around until Coen comes back at the very end of the day instead.

5 Afternoon

Enter Not

Head into the forest across the bridge north of Anca's house and follow the road until you reach an abandoned house on the left side of the path. Approach it to start the quest Enter Not, then find your way into the plague house by climbing the lower roof on the right side and dropping down inside. Grab all these things from the house:

  • Loot the corpse for the Last Confession and Figurine of St. Jude
  • Loot the small chest by the hearth for 17 Denarius, gold tableware, a recipe for mending ointment, and Knyaz Skender's Orders

You'll complete Enter Not a bit later in the day by returning the figurine to the church. For now, keep following the road north. When you reach the Blackwater Hollow shrine, do two things:

  • Use Coen's focus to inspect the abandoned wagon of peat; that's your first clue on Lazar's whereabouts

The loot in this chest is randomized, but I've found a sword better than Coen's practice sword in it each time so grab and equip whatever luck hands you there. If A Tree Falls

Deep Down

Head back south into Blackwater Hollow and pick up Lazar's trail, heading west until you find a couple wolves guarding a clearing.   2. "You don't sound convinced."
  3. "Could be a vrakhir - or an uriash?"

Loot the Forgotten Guardian and equip its Undead Warrior's Sword to replace whatever standard blade you wound up rocking. Loot the chests in this room also to grab some gold valuables to sell back in Laslea later.

Shimmy your way out of the ruins with Gavril and wrap up this section:

  • I'll walk you to Gavril. Lazar will get back safely if you don't walk with him, but it's easiest to just get teleported back to town to turn the quest in since you should be done in the bog for now.

6 Afternoon

Now that you're back in Laslea, it's time to run some errands:

  • Talk to Zdislav the elderman just north of the blacksmith.
    • I found a dead soldier: This will complete the If A Tree Falls quest
    • I found haunted ruins in the bogs: There's no reward for this, but Zdislav says he'll send soldiers to block off the ruins so that's your due diligence done.
  • Visit Mircea the blacksmith to do some shopping. You should have junk and a lot of gold valuables to sell after the ruins and the quest tour you've been on. Sell all that and treat yourself to some gear upgrades. I shelled out for the Gold-Knee Trousers and the Voyager's Ruddy Cotehardie. The Grey Knightly Gambeson is better armor but hey, sometimes fashion wins out.
  • Visit Laslea Center shrine to use some of your perk points if you haven't already. But be careful not to take any perks that spend time to unlock!

Blasphemy

Now it's time to find that missing banner for Gremla to complete the Blasphemy quest. Head back to her house near the Laslea Center shrine. Use Coen's focus to find three clues:

  • Footprints
  • Holes from a cane
  • A torn piece of banner in the dirt with blood on the back

You can go straight for the guilty party (it's Premysl) but if you want the full investigation experience, here's all the neighbors you can harangue until you find the truth:

  1. Alois, standing in front of Gremla, who has a cane but hasn't hurt his hand.
  2. Otokar, chopping wood east of Laslea gate, who has injured his hand but doesn't have a cane.
  3. Dana, sitting on a bench outside a house just west of Coen's, who's started walking with a cane but has not injured her hand either.
  4. Premysl, sitting outside the house with huge stacks of hay, just southeast of Coen's house.

Confront Premysl and decide whether he should return the banner to Gremla.

  • "Angering Brencis will put my family at risk" / "This is just an empty gesture": Coen convinces Premysl to return the banner.
  • "Maybe you're right…": Premysl keeps the banner.
  • "You haven't convinced me": Coen shames Premysl into returning the banner.

If you want to complete the prologue with all Coen's neighbors alive (for now) then tell Premysl to return the banner. Whether Premysl returns it himself or not, you'll need to head back to Gremla to complete the quest.

You can go either way on this quest though. Honestly, I think the mass and Pieter's reaction afterwards makes the most sense if it gets gruesome. Maybe Gremla is the necessary sacrifice to really show that Laslea is at a breaking point under Brencis.

7 Evening

Disturbed

Head to Crina at the graveyard and inspect Kvet's grave site for clues. You'll find footprints in the red soil to lead you towards the culprit. Use Coen's focus to follow the footprints down the hill, into the center of town, and to the right of the blacksmith's where the trail ends. Continue straight ahead towards the house in front of you and inspect a broken shovel covered in red soil outside Kostel's shed. Head inside the shed and inspect the trap door on the floor to confront Kostel and Vladimir.

You get a few yellow dialogue options with Kostel and Vladimir but they all result in essentially the same conversation. You do have an opportunity to warn Vladimir that Brencis's guards know something is afoot from how they pressed Coen at the river earlier, not that Vladimir is put off by that.

  • I'll keep this between us: You'll have to tell Crina you couldn't find the cross, bummer.
  • Give Kvet's cross back: Vlad will give up the cross for Coen to return.

Head back to Crina to return Kvet's silver cross and complete the quest:

  1. I found it lying in the bushes: You don't get anything but more heartbreak for Crina if you tell her Vladimir's the thief, so keep it to yourself.
  2. I really need to go: Sorry Crina, Coen still needs to train with Pieter, so no time for re-burying Kvet's grave.

8 Evening

Enter Not

Before you run off to train with Pieter, grab a last bit of experience by heading into the keep and the church. Talk with Father Florin to complete the Enter Not quest by handing over the Figurine of St. Jude.

Like Father, Like Son

At last, go back to Coen's house and follow Pieter up the hill to train together. He usually follows up his unblockable attack with a quick swing afterwards, to be ready to dodge and block right after. You've got a couple dialogue choices here, but they're just for the sake of roleplaying Coen because Pieter is going to get himself involved in this rebellion scheme either way. Buckle up!

Mass

If you've followed along with this walkthrough so far, here's how mass should go:

  • Gremla's blasphemous banner will hang in the church (but it won't be her hanging over the altar, which is what happens if you don't do her quest)
  • Vladimir will ask Coen whether Pieter is on board with the plan and Coen will have to say he's not sure
  • Anca asks how Esme is doing and Coen can flirt just a bit more if you want
  • Lazar is alive—he and Gavril are grateful
  • Crina says she can feel Kvet is at peace
  • Esme survives mass, thank goodness, because her death is pretty brutal if Coen brews her medicine wrong

During mass, Coen has two opportunities to speak out or fall in line. They're shown as timed choices that you have to make quickly but don't seem to affect how the night goes, so roleplay at will.

No matter what happens at mass, Pieter will muster up his revolutionary spirit at home afterwards and drag Coen off, sword in hand, to help Vladimir's crew break into the silver mines in an attempt to throw off vrakhir rule. It doesn't go well!

title: How to prepare Anca's recipe in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
During Blood of Dawnwalker 's main prologue quest, Withering Away, you'll have to prepare Anca's recipe into a medicine for your mother's anxiety, helping her overcome her fear to attend the Blood Mass that evening. Anca gives you a page of instructions to follow, but the tricksy game won't let you view them while making the medicine.
This means you're up a creek if you haven't already memorised them, and don't want to potentially load a save in the distant past just to read a sheet of paper. I'll include the instructions below, along with the friendly advice that it is very important that you make this medicine correctly.
How to prepare Anca's recipe in Blood of Dawnwalker
Use hot water Rebel Wolves Add three spoonfuls of herbs Rebel Wolves Once you arrive back at the house, your father will ask you to prepare the medicine for your mother. Unfortunately, you can't read the recipe at this point, so you have to have it memorised, or just follow the instructions below:
Choose the 'Use hot water' option
Choose the 'Add three spoonfuls of herbs' option
This follows Anca's instructions that she gave you, and will help make the correct medicine for Esme so she can have a slightly more relaxing time during the not-at-all terrifying Blood Mass that's occurring in the evening.
In case you're curious, unlike force-feeding Esme , messing up the recipe does have extremely poor consequences . I won't spoil exactly what happens, but safe to say, you'll want to ensure you get Esme the medicine she needs and that you brew it correctly. Or not. Up to you.

title: Can you beat Brencis in The Blood of Dawnwalker's prologue?
author: Sean Martin
text:
At the end of Blood of Dawnwalker 's prologue, you'll fight Brencis , the Knyaz of Vale Sangora, and quite obviously the game's main antagonist. It's one of those classic "you're not supposed to win this" boss fights, since losing to him plays a cutscene and continues the story.
But where there's a will, there's a way. Below I'll explain what happens if you beat Brencis, provide a video of fighting him, and the outcome. Be warned, this contains spoilers for some aspects of the game's ending sequence.
Can you beat Brencis in Blood of Dawnwalker's prologue?
The answer to this is a little complex—both yes and probably no. You can beat Brencis in your first fight with him provided you've learnt how to Perfect Block and dodge, though it will take a little while.
After you beat Brencis, a cutscene will play in which he effectively pulls you into hell and reveals his true form, Brencis, Grotesque Ascendant (also the final boss). Since this is still a boss fight, you theoretically should be able to beat it, but even after acquiring the strongest equipment I could on the first day, you do an incredibly small amount of damage to him, and one hit from him will invariably kill you, even if you upgrade your health in advance.
I can also confirm he gets harder in his second and third health phases, making it super challenging, and you can't quicksave, meaning you have to fight regular Brencis first for every attempt.
Basically, most players are supposed to die against this boss, as it lets you load a save when you do. Whereas if you die to regular Brencis, a cutscene plays, and the story continues, as if this is the intentional path. Presumably if you are able to defeat Brencis, Grotesque Ascendant, it lets you complete the game in the prologue, which is very funny, though we'll have to wait for someone to do it to confirm for sure.
If you want to give it a try, I recommend leveling damage (since any attack from the boss will kill you anyway) and using your vampire claws for their speed. Remember you can also press E to Shadow Step to the other side of Brencis's unblockable attacks and flurries.
You could also switch difficulty to 'Story' if you're really determined to see what happens when you beat his second phase, though be warned he is still very challenging.

title: Every romancable character in The Blood of Dawnwalker and how to have them fall fang over heels for Coen
author: Andrea Shearon
text:
Coen is certainly going through it, but Blood of Dawnwalker offers a smidge of succor by not making him face the onslaught of horrors alone. You've got three potential romance options for him—one of which seems more 'canonical' than the rest—and the vampy RPG doesn't make you choose just one. When it comes to games like this, I love to kiss and tell. So here are all three of your options for love in a breezy Blood of Dawnwalker romance guide .
Spoiler warning: While we keep details as minimal as possible, this guide follows all three romance plots through the end of the game. That includes details on how to ensure your lover shows up in the epilogue, so keep that in mind before you go skimming through the text.
How romance works in The Blood of Dawnwalker
The Blood of Dawnwalker has three romanceable characters: Anca, Lacra, and Crake. Coen isn't limited to just one partner either, so don't fret over fumbling your shot. RPG veterans won't find much out of the ordinary when it comes to wooing your fantasy lover, but here's the gist of how romance works in Blood of Dawnwalker:
The most important step is knowing where to start each romance and prioritizing chances to flirt with your love.
Requirements to woo each character mostly boil down to 'follow the questline,' so no need to worry about hidden requirements or other obscure influences.
You can romance all three characters.
Spoiler warning: It's worth highlighting that one romance is clearly favored as something long-term for Coen. I'll highlight which character gets additional screen time with minimal spoilers in the details below, but it's worth noting if you only make time to romance one option.
How to romance Anca
(Image credit: Rebel Wolves) Anca is Laslea's friendly local witch and a lifeline for people in need of medieval medical attention. The Blood of Dawnwalker prologue introduces you to her almost immediately through the main story by tasking Coen with retrieving medicine for his mum. Anca grows just the herb she needs (plus a whole lot else), and if you've got time to spare, Coen can flirt a little with her on day zero.
I'll lay out the path to romancing her below. Not all of these dialogue options are necessary for the romance, but they include flirting and confessions, so I'll include them below each step:
Complete Withering Away: Page Turner You can begin this quest by visiting Anca on the outskirts of the village in the prologue, and then hanging around to learn some latin.
When offered which book to study, choose the "How about this book with the red cover?" option and insist on it for some flirting.
Complete Echoes of Silenced Bells Note that the final choice of this quest, detailed in that guide, will not impact your ability to romance Anca.
Complete Between the Words Brew Anca a tea and choose "It's my pleasure" for some flirting.
After you read the book, choose "Always, what do you mean?" and then "Your feelings towards me - it's more than just faith" for an early all-but confession.
Complete Where Old Devils Lie At the start of the quest, choose the white dialogue option "Thank you for trying to help me" and then "That's what you see me as - a friend?" which gives you a second confirmation Anca likes you.
After you look at the map, choose the "Who knows what else I have in store for you" for more flirting.
When you sit at the mountain pool, choose the white dialogue option "Something troubling you?" and then "I care about you" to confess.
Complete Stronger Than Achilles When it comes to placing your hand in the hole, either of you seem to be able to do it, but I suggest doing it yourself so you can choose "Better me than you" option afterwards.
When Anca reveals her desire for The Font, choose "I'd do anything for you" and then "I love you". This moment is referenced later so I think it's quite important.
Let Anca use The Font While you can fully romance Anca whatever you choose at the end of Stronger Than Achilles, the happiest ending for her character is linked to letting her use The Font. You'll also get additional dialogue in the next part.
Complete the romance When you return to the inn after Stronger Than Achilles, you'll be able to discuss the fact you said "I love you" in the ruins.
Choose "I beg to differ" then "Screw decency, I want you too".
After that, Coen and Anca will kiss and the sex scene will play out.
Note: While other romanceable characters can appear in the epilogue, Anca is the one who will always appear, and who gets the most screentime. She's kind of framed as the canon romance, while Crake and Lacra are more one-night stands.
How to romance Crake
(Image credit: Rebel Wolves) Crake (or Marat) is the mortal rebel leading the Manumits against the Vrakhiri Court lording over Vale Sangora. He's well aware his adversaries wield otherworldly powers, so he (understandably) has trust issues. Win him over by demonstrating just how far you're willing to go to rise against Brencis, and Crake may show you his vulnerable side. His romance is very simple to achieve:
Complete The Firebrand You can get this quest in the prologue either by saving Vlad or investigating his house in Laslea if he dies.
Speaking to Mert at the end of the quest will start Shadows in the Woods.
Complete Shadows in the Woods Meet Sara in the woods and then Crake for the first time.
Complete Where Loyalty Lies This will let you join the Manumit rebels.
You can also start Where Loyalty Lies by going straight to the Manumit hideout in Svartrau, but you will skip some scenes.
If Vlad survived, you can also do the short Old Friends, New Friends quest by talking to him here.
Complete What Hunts the Night You can have your first intimate sharing moment with Crake when you're both hiding in the ruined house.
Complete What Moves the Dead After you save Crake from the Murohn, walk him back to the hideout, help him take his armour off, and agree to patch him up.
He'll give you the Distant Shadows quest, which is vital to his romance.
Complete Distant Shadows Crake asks you to follow an old man called Askar in Tantari.
When the soldiers start giving him trouble, you can hop out and save him.
Complete A Closer Look When you report back to Crake, he'll be angry with the outcome and will run off outside the city, starting the A Closer Look quest.
Meet him there and when you get the opportunity, choose "Hey. Nothing you say can change the way I see you". Marat will try to kiss you, you'll back off, but then you can choose to kiss him back and have sex. You'll talk a bit afterwards.
Note: As far as I can tell, the only way to get Crake to appear during the epilogue, is if you complete the final quest, Rise at Dawn, effectively following the Manumit questline through to an ending. That said, I wouldn't encourage you to choose that ending just for Crake, as you'll still get to hear about what happens to him either way.
How to romance Lacra
(Image credit: Rebel Wolves) Lacra is the only vrakhiri romance option, though her vampire status doesn't necessarily mean she's aligned with Dawnwalker's big bad. It's quite the opposite in her case, as Lacra has her own reasons for hating Brencis and is willing to find some common ground with Coen to achieve their shared goal.
Complete A Friend Like This You can get this quest by defeating Ambrus in The Gilded Gauntlet and reading the note on his corpse.
Or you can get it by helping Ocha become boss in The Heart Wants What It Wants , asking her about people who could help you, and then going to see Vicho and completing A Study in Crimson. Afterwards, Vicho will tell you about Lacra.
Complete The Song of the Mountain If you helped Ocha (mentioned above) it works out well here, as this will give you access to the Uriashi enclave and prevent any confrontations involving Lacra, though I'm sure there are other methods.
Complete Hive and Seek At that start of this quest, Lacra will blast open the cave entrance. Select "Now you're just showing off" and then "Quite so" for a bit of flirting.
Whatever choice you make regarding the Kobolds doesn't impact your ability to romance Lacra.
Complete Our Rotten Roots Choosing to veer off the path to view Lacra's memories in spite of her warnings doesn't impact your ability to romance her, but will give you more of her backstory.
I chose to invite Isbrand in, but I assume, as with Anca's Font decision, it doesn't ultimately impact your ability to romance her either way. If in doubt, invite Isbrand yourself.
Complete The Night of Horrors The most important part of this quest is eating the Mandrake flower at the end. After this, you can drink Lacra's blood, kiss, and have a very messy sex scene.
Note: The only requirement for Lacra appearing in the epilogue is completing her questline up to the final Midnight Reckoning quest. As long as you've finished all her others, she'll drop in even if you don't pursue an ending with her.

    • You can get this quest by defeating Ambrus in The Gilded Gauntlet and reading the note on his corpse.
    • Or you can get it by helping Ocha become boss in The Heart Wants What It Wants, asking her about people who could help you, and then going to see Vicho and completing A Study in Crimson. Afterwards, Vicho will tell you about Lacra.
  • Complete The Song of the Mountain
    • If you helped Ocha (mentioned above) it works out well here, as this will give you access to the Uriashi enclave and prevent any confrontations involving Lacra, though I'm sure there are other methods.
  • Complete Hive and Seek
    • At that start of this quest, Lacra will blast open the cave entrance. Select "Now you're just showing off" and then "Quite so" for a bit of flirting.
    • Whatever choice you make regarding the Kobolds doesn't impact your ability to romance Lacra.
  • Complete Our Rotten Roots
    • Choosing to veer off the path to view Lacra's memories in spite of her warnings doesn't impact your ability to romance her, but will give you more of her backstory.
    • I chose to invite Isbrand in, but I assume, as with Anca's Font decision, it doesn't ultimately impact your ability to romance her either way. If in doubt, invite Isbrand yourself.
  • Complete The Night of Horrors
    • The most important part of this quest is eating the Mandrake flower at the end. After this, you can drink Lacra's blood, kiss, and have a very messy sex scene.

Note: The only requirement for Lacra appearing in the epilogue is completing her questline up to the final Midnight Reckoning quest. As long as you've finished all her others, she'll drop in even if you don't pursue an ending with her.

title: I've spent over 80 hours in The Blood of Dawnwalker—here are my top 20 quick tips to survive Vale Sangora
author: Sean Martin
text:
Searching for some Blood of Dawnwalker tips ? Deciding what to do first in this vampiric RPG can be tough, especially if you're the kind of person who's paralysed by indecision when a game gives you a lot of freedom. You've got 30 days to save your family: everything else is pretty much anyone's game.
(Image credit: Rebel Wolves) There's no right or wrong answer. You can't really fail The Blood of Dawnwalker either, depending on how you define failure. While its time constraints form a guideline and structure to follow, where to spend that time is entirely down to you. Here's my best advice from spending 80 hours with the game, testing its many quests and choices.
1. Use the shield icon to Perfect Block
Rather than timing your block to the enemy's swing, wait for when the shield turns orange on the directional indicator. Also unlock Perfect Riposte for a guaranteed crit afterwards.
2. Take time to level up
I barely levelled in my run because I was worried about time and I made it to the end of the story with a whole 15 days left. Don't be like me.
3. Killing enemies is time-efficient
Murdering enemies you find, particularly wolves, boar, and bear bosses in the woods, is an extremely time-efficient way to get XP. In fact, it costs no time at all
4. Use towers to mark points of interest
Climbing each region tower at night will add all of its points of interest as ? symbols, including landmarks and potential quests.
5. Upgrade your vampire health ASAP
Do this with the "Endless Hunger" skill. This will make you less likely to lose control and be forced to feed on poor humans in dialogue due to only having one segment left.
6. Drink blood to increase Corruption
Animals and enemies are a great consequence-free source of blood. Some vampiric abilities are only accessible if you drink Vrakhir blood from the game's boyar bosses.
7. Grab a legendary sword early
Head to the broken bridge in northwest Briar Sloughs to start the Cursed Chasm quest. Drop down the east side of the ravine, fight some ghosts, and you'll get the legendary Durandal.
8. Spend your time wisely
You can only complete activities marked with a moon at night, and those marked with a sun in the day. Quest approaches will also change based on which it is.
9. Find new Swordmastery skills
You can get Swordmastery Manuals from Bandit and Soldier Camps or buy them from blade instructors.
10. Weapon arts are free skills
Every blue, purple, or orange (legendary) weapon has a weapon art, essentially a free skill, that you can use on cooldown. Bracers also have "claw arts" for when you're a Vrakhiri.
11. Check bookcases for Witchcraft spells
New Witchcraft Manuals come from Ancient Circles, Haunted Sites, Pilgrimage of Power quests, and Witchcraft vendors, but you can find freebies in bookcases.
12. Sell silver for big bucks
Selling silver you find exploring at the shop in Svartrau is a great way to make a lot of money very, very fast.
13. Exploration costs no time at all
Committing to activities is the only thing that costs time, so you can explore and uncover as many opportunities as you want before actually spending any.
14. Loot humans and animals for blood
The hardest part of being a vampire is healing, so make sure to loot all human and animal corpses since they have a random chance to drop blood consumables.
15. Also feed mid-combat
Remember you can use Voracious Bite mid-combat to get a bit of health back. Press Z to open active abilities and then click it when you have an activation charge.
16. Set gear presets for day and night
Click "Equipment Preview" in the right of the character screen to set different loadouts. This lets you choose passives that benefit your human side by day, and vampire side by night.
17. Scarlet Shield is very strong
This is the vampiric ability you unlock from drinking Ambrus's blood in The Gilded Gauntlet quest, and it's by far the most powerful, partially healing every time you Perfect Block.
18. White dialogue options can lead to yellow ones
I found this in Blood of Dawnwalker's romances . Sometimes skippable white dialogue options lead to otherwise inaccessible yellow "choice" options, so be thorough to avoid missing character moments.
19. Keep an eye out for new ? symbols
Though it doesn't happen often, quests sometimes appear in regions you've already "cleared". Keep an eye out for these if you want to explore every opportunity.
20. The Vrakhiri Boyar quests are some of the best
You unlock these by angering the Boyar of each region when you destroy enough of their operation, and they're some of the best quests in the game—don't skip them.

title: How to drink Vrakhir blood in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
Finding Vrakhir blood in Blood of Dawnwalker might trip you up a bit if you're looking to unlock new abilities and generally mess about as a creature of the night. While you acquire most skills in the tree naturally as you drink blood and just generally be a vampire, some specific skills only become available when you "drink Vrakhir blood" and it's not clear exactly how. Below, I'll explain where to get it, plus how to unlock all Vrakhir blood-related abilities.
How to drink Vrakhir blood in Blood of Dawnwalker
If you anger one of the Vrakhiri boyars by messing with their operation, you'll get a chance to fight them (and drink their blood) Rebel Wolves You can also get Vrakhir blood by defeating certain Murohn bosses, such as the one in the Bad Blood quest in St. Tyna's Grove Rebel Wolves You can also get Vrakhir blood from some of Xanthe's quests Rebel Wolves The main way you drink Vrakhir blood is by defeating the game's Vrakhir bosses , namely, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe, and then choosing to drink from them. Supping the blood of these three vampires unlocks different abilities, namely:
Ambrus - Scarlet Shield
Bakir - Shadowstorm
Xanthe - Blood Surge
Unlike earning skills by consuming blood and increasing your corruption, drinking from any of the Vrahkir bosses will literally give you their abilities, no skill points required. You can also drink Vrakhir blood by finding vials of it when defeating Murohn in their dens at nighttime, or through certain quests, like Xanthe's Recruiters in Tantari Woods and The Silts, or Lost Blood in St. Tyna's Grove.
These vials act a bit like manuals for Swordmastery and Witchcraft skills, letting you unlock additional levels of an ability, though you can also gain the ability by consuming these, too. Besides the three above, you can earn the remaining Vrakhir blood abilities through Lacra's questline, which you can start in Svartrau, or with a note you get after defeating Ambrus.
Piercing Shriek - By completing Our Rotten Roots quest.
Mesmerize - By eating the mandrake at the end of The Night of Horrors quest.
Otherwise, all of the other vampiric abilities unlock through raising your Corruption. Drinking Vrahkir blood will raise it considerably also, so it's a good way to fast track your growth.

title: Should you let Anca use The Font in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
author: Sean Martin
text:
Choosing whether to let Anca use The Font or claim it for yourself in Blood of Dawnwalker is tough. On the one hand, you committed a lot of time to fighting your way through an ancient ruin and it'd be nice to have something to show for it. On the other hand, you've got Anca's fate to consider. This guide will contain spoilers for Anca's questline , plus the effect of this choice. All that said, here's the impact of each option.
Should you let Anca use The Font in Blood of Dawnwalker?
(Image credit: Rebel Wolves) When you arrive in the chamber of The Font in Anca's Stronger Than Achilles quest, you'll find there's only enough tasty blood left for either you or Anca. You'll be given three choices:
"If it's alright with you - I'll use it."
"Go ahead. Make what you will with it."
"We should destroy it."
I'll run through each decision and outcome below.
1. Coen uses The Font
If Coen uses it he gains the Font of Life health regeneration perk when human (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) If you use the blood yourself, you'll gain the Font of Life passive, which regenerates human health during the day. This is a pretty decent perk, especially when Witchcraft abilities cost HP, but it's worth noting there are plenty of other ways to heal as a human and via Witchcraft skills.
Anca will accept your choice, speculating that there are likely other ways she can rid herself of her curse somewhere in the world. It won't affect your immediate romance, which will occur just after this quest. However, this decision will eventually rear its head and ultimately impact Anca's fate.
2. Anca uses The Font
This is the best outcome for Anca (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) While you won't get the passive, or any reward, this is definitely the best outcome for Anca . The Font cleanses her of the curse, most notably scrubbing away all of the red sigils etched into her arm.
Anca's newfound happiness is reflected in the subsequent romance scene where you get additional dialogue, and it ultimately means the best eventual outcome for her character.
3. You destroy The Font
You'll find the Ancient Greaves underneath The Font after you topple it over and destroy it (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) This is the worst decision of the three. After you tip over The Font, you discover a pair of fairly average legendary trousers underneath the altar. With the sheer amount of legendary armour available in Blood of Dawnwalker, this really isn't worth sacrificing Anca's happiness, or that powerful passive perk for.
However, it won't impact you romancing Anca, and the subsequent scenes will play out the same as if you used The Font yourself.

title: How to complete The Heart Wants What It Wants in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
When you stumble on The Heart Wants What It Wants in a random tavern in Blood of Dawnwalker , you might be surprised by how complex this quest can be in terms of its outcomes. The actual meat of the quest, helping an Uriashi, Ocha, and her friend, Nora, escape the clutches of Svartrau's crime lord, is pretty simple, but it can end in many different ways. Here's how to complete the quest, plus its different outcomes based on your choices.
How to complete The Heart Wants What It Wants in Blood of Dawnwalker
Use vampiric powers to get onto the balcony at night and steal Andrei's ring from his desk Rebel Wolves The ring is the correct memento for Ocha's spell Rebel Wolves Open the pig pen to distract the guard then draw the hex on the window Rebel Wolves If you go downstairs or give Ocha the wrong item, you'll have to kill Andrei, which impacts the overall outcome Rebel Wolves Once you acquire the quest from Ocha and Nora at the Altenmarkt inn, follow the map marker to Andrei's butcher shop, and enter via the balcony on the upper floor using your vampire powers. In the upper room you'll find three different mementos for Ocha's amnesia spell: a ring, a pendant, and a cleaver. The memento required for Ocha's spell is the ring .
If you'd prefer to kill Andrei instead of following Ocha's plan, go down the stairs and through the door, which will begin combat. Even though you speak to Andrei after you defeat him, no matter what you say, he'll pull sly one on you, resulting in his death. There's basically no advantage whatsoever to killing Andrei—it just impacts the options Ocha will have at the end of the quest, but more on that in the final section.
Once you have the ring, go back out onto the balcony to start a dialogue with Ocha, who's waiting below. Make sure to give her the ring. If you give her the wrong memento, the spell will fail, and you and Ocha will have to kill Andrei , which results in the same outcome as mentioned above.
Now simply distract the guard by opening the pig pen and then draw the hex on the outside of the butcher's shop. Andrei will smash his brains out against a wall, and Ocha will explain this is what she meant by "empty his head." Human words are hard, apparently. She'll ask you to meet her outside the city, starting the final section.
Deciding Ocha's fate in Blood of Dawnwalker
What you tell Ocha by the river will decide where she goes next (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) You'll meet Ocha outside by the river, where she'll ask you to catch some crayfish so you two can eat. Ocha has two choices she can make based upon your advice and whether you killed Andrei or he killed himself. If you killed Andrei:
Ocha goes travelling with Nora, but will stick around a while to teach you Swordmastery.
Ocha goes back to the Uriashi settlement in the mountains.
If Andrei killed himself via the spell:
Ocha stays in the city and becomes a crime boss with Nora. She sets up shop in Andrei's hideout, teaches Swordmastery, and gives you a line to Vacho, beginning the Study in Crimson quest. This outcome is also useful in certain future dialogue challenges in Svartrau.
Ocha goes back to the Uriashi settlement in the mountains.
Ocha will choose these based upon what dialogue options you pick. For either of the first options listed above, choose:
"Do you miss home?"
"New things can be exciting, sure."
"Our neighbours helped a bit."
For either of the second options listed above, choose:
"Do you miss home"
"Meh. Nothing better than homemade food!"
"Our neighbours helped a bit"
Either way, you'll receive the Broad Swing Swordmastery manual as quest reward. Ocha's name will also be useful later in getting you access to the Uriashi settlement you visit in Lacra's quest, Song of the Mountain, even if she doesn't go back there.
Presumably, if Ocha goes home, she can also teach you Swordmastery skills at the settlement, but I haven't been able to confirm that.

title: How to complete A Bulwark Against Darkness in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
Receiving the A Bulwark Against Darkness quest in Blood of Dawnwalker is a bit of a surprise, coming, as it does, from a smuggler who's been sent to infiltrate Vale Sangora just to give you this message. Your mysterious benefactor details a special set of armour that can help you in your fight against Brencis, though only if you find all of the components for yourself—what a cheapskate. I'll explain each component location below and how to forge the legendary Arbiter set at the end of it.
How to complete A Bulwark Against Darkness in Blood of Dawnwalker
You'll get given an armor component list by a courier after you reforge Mihai's silver sword (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) After you read the mysterious letter and the list of armour components, you'll have to track down all four using the clues the list gives you. Here's where to find each.
Relic of a Saint location
You can grab the Saint's Tibia from a corpse at the bottom of a ladder in St. Tyna's Convent (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) There are multiple relics you can grab during the game, but the easiest is the Saint's Tibia, which you can find in St. Tyna's Convent during Anca's Echoes of Silenced Bells quest. When you arrive in the big inner convent courtyard (where the majority of the quest takes place), look for a corpse below a ladder on the west side of the area. You can also use the Relic of St. Tyna itself, but you'd be sacrificing a purple rarity amulet.
The other relics you can find are:
If you complete Vicho's Study in Crimson quest in Svartrau, you can purchase a legendary relic from him.
During Lacra's The Night of Horrors quest, you'll find this legendary relic with a severed arm while exploring the swamp.
Either way, your best bet is using that Saint's Tibia item instead and saving your precious jewellery.
Bundle of Silk Threads location
You can buy Silk Threats from the Sanzhana merchant if you pursue their questline (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) This one is a bit more elaborate to acquire and will cost around 6,000 denari. First off, you'll have to complete the Good Home quest you get on the west side of the Svartrau Outskirts north of the city. This introduces the Sanzhani and starts the Letters to Lunka quest. Flask of Quiksilver location
You can find the Flask of Quiksilver at the top of Aurelius's tower in the south of The Silts Rebel Wolves It's on a table to the left of the room after you defeat Aurelius Rebel Wolves This item is on the top floor of Aurelius's Tower in the southwest of The Silts region, south of Turtle Rock shrine and then the Aurelius's Tower shrine. You'll have to climb the tower, fight Svetlana, The Dark Prodigy, and then face Aurelius on the top floor, starting the Home Sweet Home quest. Moult of a Large Lizard location
You can find the lizard moult in a cave filled with Tatzelwurms in Briar Sloughs bog Rebel Wolves Look for a small cave entrance and find the moult on the floor after you defeat the lizards Rebel Wolves This is the easiest of the items to grab. You can find the Uriash blacksmith in the northwest of Briar Sloughs Rebel Wolves You'll have to perform a ritual and fight some ghosts to forge the legendary armor variant Rebel Wolves Once you have all the components, go to see the Uriash Hermit blacksmith in northwest Briar Sloughs. I'm pretty sure you need to reforge St. Mihai's Silver Sword to get the A Bulwark Against Darkness quest, so you should have already met and worked with her. If, for some reason, you haven't, head through the forest to the Uriashi Hermitage shrine in the northwest of the region.
Each time you give her a component, you'll get a new piece of the Arbiter armour. title: The Blood of Dawnwalker - best settings to tweak
author: Dave James
text:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is a punishing game. And not just because of the divisive time-as-a-resource-to-be-managed side of things (or the almost impossible to resist desire to shift 'the' around in the title) but because it will slay your PC in terms of performance. We've covered the fact that in order to hit any of the performance level system requirements you have to enable upscaling in Balanced mode , but it's also worth noting that those system requirements are a little generous, too.
I've been testing Dawnwalker for the past week or so, with a few different setups, and in those forests of Carpathia you're going to either need some more beefy hardware to hit Rebel Wolves' proposed frame rate targets or compromise on those graphics settings.
Which is where I'm coming in here, aiming to help you get the highest frame rate out of your rig without sacrificing the actual look of the game.
And, actually The Blood of Dawnwalker does pretty well even down at the lower end of the graphics settings, still looking relatively crisp and with a detailed open world for you to explore to your vampyric heart's content.
As a representative system, I've picked out Rebel Wolves' mid-range spec, the one designed to net you 60 fps at 1440p. That's an Nvidia RTX 4060 graphics card, with an eight-core AMD CPU at its heart, of which I've selected the AMD Ryzen 7 7700X . This should theoretically be enough to get you that 60 fps target using the High preset in the games.

Dropping that DLSS setting down to Performance—essentially running the game at 720p—will only net you another 6 fps on average
But that is very much going to depend on where you are. Right from the outset you will find yourself running around the dense forests, either with a sword in your hand or with fangs and claws at the ready. And those forests immediately tank your frame rates.
I've picked a repeatable run in Briar Sloughs, through the forest, out into the open and then back in for a scrap with a big ol' slimy monster. And you are lucky to be hitting an average 50 fps at 1440p with High settings even with DLSS set to Balanced.
Interestingly, dropping that DLSS setting down to Performance—essentially running the game at 720p—will only net you another 6 fps on average. And although Nvidia has gotten pretty good with the stability of its Performance and Ultra Performance modes, there's still a lot of noise around the foliage in this game. And there's a lot of that.
I've run the game on AMD GPUs, too, and even with FSR 4 enabled in the game I've found the Ultra Performance mode to be even more noisy, with an obvious shimmer in rock textures, too. That initially made me think I was looking at an FSR 3 implementation. You also get a fair bit of fringing around the main character as you're travelling around the gameworld, even with DLSS set to relatively high levels.
Which settings to tweak?
High preset vs. custom
Image comparison of the 'High' preset against our own custom settings.
High preset
Custom preset
So, what settings should you compromise on to actually be able to hit that 60 fps standard? I've found four settings that combined will give you a decent chunk of extra performance back without harming the visual fidelity too much. These are the same settings I've had to compromise in order to get good 4K/60 performance at (more or less) the Ultra preset on Rebel Wolves' recommended graphics card, so they do scale.
Knocking each of Shadow, Light, Foliage, and Detail Quality down a notch to Medium I managed to hit 57 fps on average during my run, but taking Shadow Quality back to Low finally got me to a 62 fps average. Shadows is a pretty typical resource hog for an Unreal Engine 5 game, and when there are this many shadows owing to the level of foliage detail in the forests, that's always going to have an impact on your frame rate.

But even at low settings, the shadows still look pretty decent, especially when you're hackin' and slashin' around at pace. They do have a tendency to pop-in a little more noticeably during motion compared to the higher shadow settings, but I didn't find it too distracting during actual gameplay.
You do get less 'stuff' on the forest floors by cutting the Foliage quality back, but I kinda don't see that as a massive miss. Especially as for a large part what you're losing is the kinda scattered hay aesthetic.
It must be said, however, that these numbers are purely an average and there will still be frame drops below the 60 fps mark. I have another benchmark run I've been testing with that's even more punishing, which is a multi-character fight at night, and even with these settings pared back that test drops the average frame rate down to just 53 fps.
So what's a mid-range GPU owner to do?
Frame Generation
(Image credit: Rebel Wolves) Yes, right before launch, Rebel Wolves has added an experimental Frame Generation setting to the game. Covering both AMD and Nvidia implementations, you are able to use 2x Frame Gen to help boost the smoothness of your game. I almost wrote 'performance' there and had to catch myself.
The interpolated frames of either FSR or DLSS Frame Gen cannot really be called extra performance; they are simply smoothing out your experience to make a lower frame rate feel far more comfortable.
But while it's experimental, I'd say it's definitely worth giving it a go if your system is capable. Any modern AMD or Nvidia card from the last two generations will deliver a decent Frame Gen experience, and the RTX 4060 performs admirably. Generally I'd want a base 60 fps for Frame Gen to feel good in-game, but the 50 fps average I've got in the High preset with DLSS Balanced is good enough here.

Even though it is 2x Frame Gen, you are not, however, doubling your effective frame rate. With the feature enabled I have a jump from that 50 fps mark to 73 fps on average.
And, visually, it's still pretty solid. I mentioned earlier that there is a level of fringing around the main character no matter what setting you're using, but it did feel more obvious when running with Frame Gen enabled. There is also some artifacting when you quickly pan the camera around in highly detailed scenes, but mostly only when you're looking for it.
Generally the most punishing thing for Frame Generation is the added PC latency you get from enabling the feature, but I've only measured an extra 4 ms of PCL from turning it on with the RTX 4060. And the extra smoothness you get, alongside a higher graphical preset, is absolutely worth that trade off.
I will admit, I'm a pretty comfortable advocate for Frame Generation, though with Dawnwalker I'd maybe suggest that if you're getting 60 fps+ without it that for clarity alone I think I'd leave it off. But, if I'm talking about getting that extra little bit of smoothness from an RTX 4060, I would absolutely have that feature enabled.

title: How to complete Forge It Anew in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
The Forge It Anew quest in Blood of Dawnwalker sees you trying to reforge St. Mihai's Silver Sword after you acquired it during A Monk and a Saint. Vrakhiri aren't very fond of silver, as you've likely surmised, so this sword will make for a potent vampire-slaying tool. You'll have to track down the missing sword shards and then a blacksmith to put them all together, so here's where to look.
How to complete Forge It Anew in Blood of Dawnwalker
Read the note in St. Mihai's coffin after you defeat him to start the quest (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) There are three sword shards located in Kobold nests around Vale Sangora that you need to find before you can reforge the Sword of St. Mihai.
First sword shard location
The first shard is in a Kobold nest in the northeast of the Maragir Wealds Rebel Wolves Defeat the Kobolds then grab the shard from the broken cross Rebel Wolves The first sword shard is located in the northeast corner of the Maragir Wealds , to the northeast of the Upper Maragir Wealds shrine, across the river. You'll find a cave, along with a trail you can follow, which begins the Forge It Anew: Do Not Disturb quest. Pursue the trail into the Kobold den, kill them, and then take the shard from the broken cross. There should also be a cave painting map here that will give you quest markers for the other shard locations if you examine it.
Second sword shard location
The second shard is located in the north of the Rockfalls region Rebel Wolves You're looking for a Kobold nest with a big white X above it Rebel Wolves Defeat the corrupted Kobold, Munch-Munch, then grab the shard Rebel Wolves The second sword shard is in the north of the Rockfalls region , east over the mountains from the Westridge Outpost shrine, though actually accessible from the east if you head through the forest. It's also directly southwest from the Giant's Pawns shrine.
You'll find a Kobold nest with a white X above the entrance, and inside, a corrupted Kobold called Munch-Munch, starting the Forge It Anew: Hostile Takeover quest. This is a fairly tricky boss who poisons on hit, but once defeated, you can grab the sword shard from the nest. Again, there's a map here that will mark the other shard locations.
Third sword shard location
The final shard is located in a Kobold nest in the south of St. Tyna's Grove Rebel Wolves Clues at the nest will point you to a soldier camp in the northwest of the Tantari Woods region Rebel Wolves Defeat the troops and grab it from the chest in the tent Rebel Wolves The final sword shard is in south St. Tyna's Grove , directly southeast from the Crossroads Inn where you meet Anca for the Echoes of Silenced Bells quest. Head south from the Crossroads Inn shrine outside, then take the left road going up into the hills to find the Kobold nest, beginning the Forge It Anew: Executive Order quest.
Searching the den, you'll find that the sword shard has been taken to one of Xanthe's camps to the west in The Silts. Follow the marker here, defeat the enemies, and grab the final shard from the small chest in the main tent.
Where to find the Uriashi blacksmith
You can find the Uriash blacksmith in northwest Briar Sloughs Rebel Wolves You'll have to undertake a ritual to the northwest once you bring her all the shards Rebel Wolves Fight your way into the ancient ruins and quench the sword to get its legendary variant Rebel Wolves Now you have all the shards, you need a blacksmith to put them together. I'd already met the Uriashi blacksmith before this point in the quest, so I'm unsure if it makes you find them, but either way, you want to head to the Uriashi Hermitage shrine in northwest Briar Sloughs , through the forest and up the hill.
Here you'll find a big standing stone in the middle of a circle, and a lone hornless Uriashi, who will agree to reforge the sword if you speak to her. The final step is heading up the hill into an ancient ruin, defeating some enemies, and quenching St. Mihai's Sword in a rather cursed looking red orb of magic. With this, you'll gain the legendary Imbued Sword of St. Mihai. It has an extremely good weapon art which actually changes depending whether it's day or night—I personally prefer the AoE daytime version.

The Forge It Anew quest in Blood of Dawnwalker sees you trying to reforge St. Mihai's Silver Sword after you acquired it during A Monk and a Saint. Vrakhiri aren't very fond of silver, as you've likely surmised, so this sword will make for a potent vampire-slaying tool. You'll have to track down the missing sword shards and then a blacksmith to put them all together, so here's where to look.

How to complete Forge It Anew in Blood of Dawnwalker

There are three sword shards located in Kobold nests around Vale Sangora that you need to find before you can reforge the Sword of St. Mihai.

First sword shard location

The first sword shard is located in the northeast corner of the Maragir Wealds, to the northeast of the Upper Maragir Wealds shrine, across the river. You'll find a cave, along with a trail you can follow, which begins the Forge It Anew: Do Not Disturb quest. Pursue the trail into the Kobold den, kill them, and then take the shard from the broken cross. There should also be a cave painting map here that will give you quest markers for the other shard locations if you examine it.

Second sword shard location

The second sword shard is in the north of the Rockfalls region, east over the mountains from the Westridge Outpost shrine, though actually accessible from the east if you head through the forest. It's also directly southwest from the Giant's Pawns shrine.

You'll find a Kobold nest with a white X above the entrance, and inside, a corrupted Kobold called Munch-Munch, starting the Forge It Anew: Hostile Takeover quest. This is a fairly tricky boss who poisons on hit, but once defeated, you can grab the sword shard from the nest. Again, there's a map here that will mark the other shard locations.

Third sword shard location

The final sword shard is in south St. Tyna's Grove, directly southeast from the Crossroads Inn where you meet Anca for the Echoes of Silenced Bells quest. Head south from the Crossroads Inn shrine outside, then take the left road going up into the hills to find the Kobold nest, beginning the Forge It Anew: Executive Order quest.

Searching the den, you'll find that the sword shard has been taken to one of Xanthe's camps to the west in The Silts. Follow the marker here, defeat the enemies, and grab the final shard from the small chest in the main tent.

Where to find the Uriashi blacksmith

Now you have all the shards, you need a blacksmith to put them together. I'd already met the Uriashi blacksmith before this point in the quest, so I'm unsure if it makes you find them, but either way, you want to head to the Uriashi Hermitage shrine in northwest Briar Sloughs, through the forest and up the hill.

Here you'll find a big standing stone in the middle of a circle, and a lone hornless Uriashi, who will agree to reforge the sword if you speak to her. The final step is heading up the hill into an ancient ruin, defeating some enemies, and quenching St. Mihai's Sword in a rather cursed looking red orb of magic. With this, you'll gain the legendary Imbued Sword of St. Mihai. It has an extremely good weapon art which actually changes depending whether it's day or night—I personally prefer the AoE daytime version.

title: How to complete Home Sweet Home in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
Finding a way to escape the neverending nightmare of Home Sweet Home in Blood of Dawnwalker took me longer than I'd care to admit. Like me, you probably thought defeating Aurelius in The Silts Tower would be a quick in-out jobbie, but now you're trapped in a grindy dream sequence defeating endless tides of spectres.
Fear not, though, there is a way to escape the dream, and I'll explain how below. If you're here and haven't encountered this quest yet, firstly, why? Secondly, leave now so as not to spoil yourself.
How to complete Home Sweet Home in Blood of Dawnwalker
You need to investigate the well in the village area where you rescue your siblings from ghosts Rebel Wolves You'll speak to your reflection and open up a new route to take through the dream Rebel Wolves In the church, interact with the yellow-marked figures based on what the priest is saying Rebel Wolves After you run through the dream sequence once, having breakfast with your family, watching as they're kidnapped by a flying monster, then saving them all and heading to the church, you'll realise you're stuck in a time loop. In fact, I completed this whole sequence twice, after which, even the same dialogue repeats.
To break free from this neverending cycle, you need to interact with the well in the village . You can only do this after you've completed the whole dream sequence once. On the second runthrough, when you save your siblings from the spectres in the village, instead of continuing up the hill to your father, turn right in the area where you fought them to spot a well you can interact with. This sequence will open up a new route you can take.
You'll then find yourself in a funeral scene in a church and will have to examine the characters present in the correct order as the priest reads his sermon. The correct order is:
Alin (in the coffin)
Esme (Coen's mum on the right)
Coen (the small child on the left)
After this, it's all smooth sailing. You'll leave the church and examine a clearing, and then head down to the river, where the dream concludes and you're able to escape back into reality and Aurelius's Tower in The Silts.

title: How to complete Letters to Lunka in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
The Letters to Lunka quest in Blood of Dawnwalker is a sneaky way to get a bit more intel about what's happening with Coen's family in Griefberg Castle. As you likely discovered in the Good Home quest, these fairies can spirit themselves into the dungeon and whisper messages in Lunka's ear. If you help out the Sanzhani around the map, you can ask all remaining questions—here's how it works.
How to complete Letters to Lunka in Blood of Dawnwalker
You can send one message to Lunka for each Sanzhani you help (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) After you finish the Good Home quest and accept your reward of sending your first letter to Lunka, you can send four more letters, one per Sanzhani quest you complete around Vale Sangora.
Whenever you send a new letter, a new quest will appear for you to complete, so don't forget to send one back at the main burrow each time. The order these quests appear on the map is linked to which letters you send , but either way, it'll be one of the following locations marked by a ? below:
Burrow Sorrows
The Burrow Sorrows quest is in the forest in the northwest of The Rockfalls region (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) This quest marker shows up in the northwest of the Rockfalls region, south of the Giant's Pawns shrine in the north, and southwest of Parlita. You have to help a Sanzhani reclaim a nest filled with Kobolds.
Pearly and Precious
The Pearly and Precious quest is in the north of Boar's Back by the river (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) The next quest marker is by the river separating Boar's Back with Briar Sloughs, northeast of Parlita, and directly south of Stoneward Post where you likely freed Mert . She'll ask you to kill some bandit so she can take their teeth. This quest also unlocks the Sanzhani trader, who sells the Bundle of Silk Threads you need for the A Bulwark Against Darkness quest. She also buys teeth you collect from dead enemies for good money.
Come Hither
The Come Hither quest is in the east of The Silts region (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) This third quest marker is located in the east of The Silts region, north of the Vedera Marsh Guardpost shrine, and northwest of Tantari Tower. This is a simple one—the Sanzhani just wants you to kill a Murohn that invaded one of their burrows.
Tiny Dancer
The Tiny Dancer quest is right in the middle of Svartrau (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) The final Sanzhani quest marker is located in Svartrau, in the upper room of a townhouse right in the middle of the city, south of Altenmarkt. You'll need to be in vampire form to reach it, but once inside, grab the key from the desk and free the fairy from the cage. You can also go into the next room to loot the man's silver, but you will have to kill him if so.
With that, you've completed every Sanzhani quest in Vale Sangora. Head back to the burrow to send your final letter, and to get a special reward— the tsarina will refund an entire day's worth of time for you .

title: Should you invite Ambrus in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
author: Sean Martin
text:
Deciding whether to invite Ambrus in is a tough choice in Blood of Dawnwalker , especially as you don't really know what "invite" means in this context. This rogue-ish Vrakhir certainly deserves hell for all the atrocities he committed bleeding Vale Sangora's subjects, but maybe there's more to him than meets the eye. Obviously, this guide will contain spoilers as to the immediate and eventual impact of this choice, so leave now if you don't want to know.
Should you invite Ambrus in Blood of Dawnwalker?
You'll have to decide whether to invite Ambrus if you drink his blood (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) If you invite Ambrus in, the main consequence is that he'll talk to you throughout the rest of the game . I'm not talking full blown dialogue, but he'll essentially make comments as a voice inside your head, about stuff you're doing, such as when you make a choice, or in combat. In fact, there's one Ambrus comment at a particular moment (I won't spoil it) that made me laugh so much I consider it well worth inviting him just for that.
Does it have any consequences? Basically, no. The main impact is that Ambrus will help you a bit in the final boss, but he can also be turned against you in the fight itself, so it's a 'swings and roundabouts' situation. The best way to decide is whether you think Ambrus deserves a shot at redemption, or if you want him to spend an eternity of torment in Anachora (vampire hell). The same applies to the other Vrakhiri boyars you can kill in Blood of Dawnwalker.
Inviting Ambrus doesn't impact abilities, Corruption, or vampiric powers either. As long as you drank his Vrakhir blood (which, if you're inviting him, you did) you'll get his Scarlet Shield ability either way, and honestly, it's one of the best in the game, healing you whenever you Perfect Block.

title: Should you kill the soldiers at the mill in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
author: Sean Martin
text:
Deciding whether you should kill the soldiers at Mert's Mill during Blood of Dawnwalker 's The Firebrand quest looks like a minor choice at first, but a life does hang on it. After investigating Vlad's house in Laslea, you'll be directed to the mill in the region to the south. When you arrive, though, you'll be confronted by a bunch of soldiers, and you'll have to decide what to do about them.
Should you kill the soldiers or leave them be in Blood of Dawnwalker?
If you arrive at night, the soldiers will ambush you, but you can talk your way out of it (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) During The Firebrand quest, if you arrive at the farm during the night, you'll be ambushed by some soldiers who demand your identity. You can talk your way out of it by saying "I'm Mirto" , but if you kill them Mert's wife Renna will emerge and tell you that you've made a grave mistake and that she'll be punished as a rebel collaborator, considering Mert is already in prison at Stoneward Post.
If you come during the day instead, Renna will pretend you've come to fix the cart. She will explain what's going on and ask you not to kill the soldiers hiding in the barn, again, to avoid making her appear to be a rebel. She's totally wrong, though. You should absolutely kill the soldiers in the barn because otherwise Renna will be killed while you're off trying to free Mert from prison. If you didn't kill the soldiers, Renna's corpse will be lying in the middle of the farm when you get back from your rescue.
I haven't tested whether there are consequences for putting off this quest for too long, so I'd suggest getting Mert out as soon as possible. After jailbreaking Mert, you tell him to flee with Renna to the Svartrau Almshouse and leave the area. If you killed the soldiers, you won't find Renna's corpse when you return to the farm, meaning they presumably got out safely.
You can meet Mert again at the Almshouse in Svartrau Cathedral's complex later, so be sure to check in on him when passing through.

title: Should you force feed Esme in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
author: Sean Martin
text:
Deciding whether to force feed Coen's mum in Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the initial choices you'll encounter, but if you're like me, you may pause over it a while wondering how much it's going to impact. The game's prologue has only just started in earnest, and this is the first proper decision you encounter after all. So, here's what happens based on either choice and which I recommend picking.
Should you force feed Coen's mum in Blood of Dawnwalker?
Trying to force feed Esme is indeed bad (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) While Esme indeed does need to eat—how else is she going to make lots of lovely blood for mass in the evening—force feeding her doesn't help the situation. If you choose the "Alright. Let's try" option, Coen will pick up the spoon and try to force feed Esme, but this results in her smacking the spoon aside and then essentially bursting into tears, leaving your dad, Pieter, feeling very sorry about what he tried to do.
Choosing the "I won't feed her against her will" option instead sees your father try to force feed her, but she also still bats the spoon out of his hand. It's the same result, but this way she at least seems less distressed with the outcome. This decision has no long term impact —it's more just a chance to dip your toes in the game's choice mechanics before some proper decisions later.
So yes, not trying to force feed her is the way to go if you don't want to feel bad. Either way, your father will ask you to head to Anca's to get some herbs so your mother can make it through the evening's blood mass.

title: How to complete Where Loyalty Lies in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
Completing Where Loyalty Lies is the first big step in aligning yourself with a faction in Blood of Dawnwalker . Until now, you've likely been taking the fight to Brencis yourself, though maybe you decided to free Mert out of the goodness of your heart. But to join the Manumits, you'll have to prove your commitment to the cause by raising your infamy, a system you may not have interacted with much until now.
How to complete Where Loyalty Lies in Blood of Dawnwalker
Angering and defeating a Vrakhiri boyar (like Ambrus) is a great way to earn infamy Rebel Wolves Crushing Soldier Camps is a very time-effective way of getting infamy since they only cost one cycle Rebel Wolves The same goes for the Soldier Pickets that start appearing when you reach infamy Level 2 Rebel Wolves You'll need to raise your infamy level to Notorious in order to join the Manumits, which is the fourth (IV) level on the court's infamy track, which you can see in the 'Court' tab of the menu. Your best bet for raising infamy is:
Complete named Vrakhir quests in any of the regions , such as Ambrus's Cellars, Ambrus's Transports, Ambrus's Collectors, or Ambrus's Prisoners, all of which are available in the regions just after you leave Laslea, such as in Briar Sloughs, Maragir Wealds, and St. Tyna's Grove. Other Vrahkir boyars have their own quests in other regions, which are similarly named.
Defeat one of the Vrakhiri boyars . Completing named Vrakhir quests will increase their anger, which you can see if you hover over their portrait in the court menu. A good way to do this is by completing every quest in a particular node, such as destroying all of Ambrus's blood cellars. Once you anger them sufficiently, you'll get a quest to defeat them, such as The Gilded Gauntlet for Ambrus.
Destroying Soldier Camps and Soldier Pickets : Soldier Camps are an incredibly time-efficient way to earn infamy. They don't increase a boyar's anger as much but they only consume one hourglass. They also generally reward you with a Swordsmastery manual . When you reach infamy level 2, Military Checkpoints will appear, which are equally time-efficient.
I'd recommend a mixture, destroying Soldier Camps in Ambrus's regions to unlock those abilities, but then also deal with some of Ambrus's operations to anger him enough, fight him, and gain a big chunk of infamy there. Either that, or go to a completely different region and anger one of the other boyars instead, though enemies in these will be a bit harder.
Once you reach Notorious infamy, you can head to Svartrau and meet up with Sara to continue the Manumit questline.

title: How to complete Blasphemy in The Blood of Dawnwalker
author: Sean Martin
text:
The Blasphemy quest is one of the most impactful in Blood of Dawnwalker 's prologue, since it impacts the Blood Mass at the end of the day. When you find Gremla, bemoaning the theft of her tapestry, she explains that she took on that task of weaving a vampiric banner for the Knyaz, and that Brencis won't be pleased if she can't get it back.
It's easy enough to see the writing on the wall as to the outcome for not completing this one. However, the quest's second section, which sees you searching for the culprit, is actually quite tough. Below, I'll run through the whole quest, plus I've included details as to the outcome and rewards for getting Gremla's tapestry back, or keeping the thief's secret.
How to complete Blasphemy in Blood of Dawnwalker
Investigate the loom in Gremla's house Rebel Wolves Investigate the footprints and walking stick trail leading to the torn scrap Rebel Wolves Examine the torn scrap and find the blood stain Rebel Wolves After you speak to Gremla at her house in Laslea, you need to use Focus Mode (right click) to do some investigating:
Use Focus Mode to inspect the weaving loom in her house
Inspect the trail of footprints and the cane trail around the side of the building
Inspect the torn corner of tapestry at the end of the footprint trail and turn it around to spot the blood on it
This leads Coen to conclude that the thief cut their hand when they took the tapestry and that they also walk with a cane, so you'll have to search Laslea to find someone who matches the description.
The culprit with the walking stick is in the northeast corner of Laslea Rebel Wolves Find Premsyl sitting outside his house Rebel Wolves There are three villagers who walk with canes, but you're looking for Premysl, who lives in the house at the most northeasterly point of the search area , marked on the screenshot above. He should be sitting outside his house.
Should you make Premsyl return the tapestry?
If you let Premsyl keep the banner it spells bad news for Gremla (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) After you ask about his injured hand and cane, you can confront Premysl, and he reveals that he took the tapestry because it's an abomination to hang it in the church because of the nightmarish scene it depicts. You can either:
Convince Premsyl to give it back : He's easy to convince, just don't choose the "Maybe you're right…" option. Report back to Gremla and you'll get some money and XP. In the Blood Mass in the evening, the nightmarish banner will be hanging in the church and the villagers will react with horror.
Agree with him and he'll keep the tapestry : If you choose the "Maybe you're right…" option when he tries to convince you to keep it secret, he will, and you'll get the Daylight Amulet from him as a reward. In the evening, instead of the tapestry, Gremla will be killed and hung in the church.
You might be thinking that killing Gremla is worth a Superior Amulet, but you'll definitely find other amulets that are better before very long. Basically, if you want to save Gremla, don't feel obligated to let her die just to get the reward, when you can find lots of amulets in the game by just searching around, defeating enemies, and looting.
That said, Gremla isn't a very important character, and this doesn't seem to have an impact beyond the prologue, so do as your heart dictates.
